Furthermore, the project successfully collaborated with local government units to engineer and certify the university’s first official flood evacuation routes. Keystroke Injection Detection System using Naive Bayes Algorithm and Pattern Recognition. A USB device is normally used to connect devices to computers or store data. However, a sophisticated device emerged that mim- ics keystroke inputs into the computer system. These devices are called BadUSB's. These are USB Devices that are programmed to execute keystroke payloads and launch then onto the computer system. To counteract against this threat, particularly keystroke injection attacks, this paper introduces a Keystroke Injection Detec- tion System (KI.D.S). Employing sophisticated pattern recognition and the Naive Bayes algorithm, the system scrutinizes user key- stroke patterns to differentiate between authentic and manipulated input. Leveraging the user-friendly and effective nature of Naive Bayes, the system classifies data after training on a dataset of typ- ical typing behaviors. The system constructs a robust model that identifies anomalies indicative of keystroke injection attempts by analyzing temporal and spatial keystroke characteristics through advanced pattern recognition algorithms. With an efficiency rate of 98%, K.I.D.S exhibits low false-positive rates, real-time detection, and adaptability to evolving attack vectors. Experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness across various scenarios, further en- hancing cyber security protocols. The combination of Naive Bayes and pattern recognition proves to be a promising approach for developing reliable and accurate keystroke injection detection sys- tems.

An effective Records Management System (RMS) is critical for organizational accountability, transparency, and efficiency. This study evaluated the RMS at Camarines Sur Polytechnic Colleges (CSPC) using the Delone and McLean Success Model, focusing on system quality, information quality, service quality, intention to use, user satisfaction, and net benefits. A mixed-methods approach was employed, gathering data through surveys and interviews with administrators, basic users, and IT experts. Results were analyzed using a weighted mean to assess perceptions based on the six dimensions. Information quality was high in accuracy (4.09), completeness (4.03), and relevance (4.01) but required improvement in timeliness (3.99). Service quality excelled in empathy (4.16) and assurance (4.08) but showed lower responsiveness (3.58) and reliability (3.66). User satisfaction was positive, contributing to the intention to continue using the system. Net benefits reflected the RMS's role in enhancing organizational efficiency and decision-making. Identified areas for improvements include adding barcode scanning, dropdown menus, tooltips, and document classification. Suggestions also focus on removing resigned users, updating directories, enabling real-time notifications, conducting workshops, and ensuring continuous updates. These recommendations suggest future efforts to optimize tracking and indexing processes, refine system functionalities, and develop an improved version to further enhance organizational outcomes.

Pre-proposal text:
RFID-BASED INTEGRATED COMPUTER LABORATORY EQUIPMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. The College of Computer Studies under Camarines Sur Polytechnic Colleges seeks to employ an easy automation of recording, inventory and monitoring of Computer Laboratory Equipment as much as possible to aid the existing manual process on Computer Laboratories. Based on the findings the following are the problems encountered on manual recording, inventory, monitoring and tracking of borrowed equipment; The data of borrowed equipment is not being recorded, record book is unorganized, recording of Equipment is time consuming and an un-organized list of equipment. With these, this study is conducted to develop a system that will automate the recording, inventory, monitoring and tracking of borrowed equipment to which it was the basis on the development of the RFID-Based Integrated Computer Laboratory Equipment Management System. Generally, this study used a Descriptive-Quantitati ve form of research to determine the problems in the existing manual process on Computer Laboratory. The respondents of this study were the Computer Laboratory Staff, student and other computer laboratory related personnel under College of Computer Studies. In gathering data, researcher made questionnaires, used for the survey and observation. The data gathered were analyze and interpreted using Weighted Mean. The analysis of the data showed that the developed system was highly acceptable in terms of functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, maintainability, and portability. Furthermore, the analysis showed that the performance of the developed RFID-Based system was highly acceptable. Therefore, it is reasonable to implement the RFID-Based Integrated Computer Laboratory Equipment Management System.

Pre-proposal text:
Design of a Web-based Platform for Management and Analysis of Disaster and Emergency Report in Nabua, Camarines Sur. Technology in the modern world is rapidly changing and companies can transition of manual-based activities and move to use digital systems that are more efficient. The purpose of the study was to design an online system of disaster and emergency reports management and analysis in the Municipality of Nabua, Camarines Sur. In this regard, the researchers have utilized the User-Centered Design (UCD) tool corresponding to ISO 9241-210 to make sure that the web-based platform directly responded to issues and needs of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO). The researchers optimized the interface of the platform and general functionalities of the site through survey, interview, usability, and expert review to enhance accessibility, readability, and data sorting. Results showed that the developed system improved the management of disaster reports greatly with high rates being accepted in functionality, satisfaction and usability, and that users rated that the workflows became smoother, the process of retrieving the information became quicker and the accuracy of documented reports was improved. Specifically, digitalization enabled the employees of MDRRMO to work more on decision-making and response to emergencies instead of doing the same encoding over and over again. The research proposes the extension of the platform by real-time capabilities, automated analytics, and mobile capabilities to enhance the disaster preparedness of Nabua. Future researchers can also replicate or expand the system to other municipalities to investigate how a single digital platform can facilitate the process of disaster and emergency operations across Camarines Sur.

The researchers perform the non-observation participant for the developed system through functional testing. The overall function of the system during the first iteration was moderately functional. Security Testing yielded 0.89 (Low Risk), which confirms strong controls were established to keep sensitive institutional information safe. This study integrates Robotic Process Automation (RPA) through Microsoft Power Automate Desktop (PAD) to automate selected routines in the Camarines Sur Polytechnic Colleges Library, specifically within the INFOLIB and KOHA systems. Guided by the Business Process Management (BPM) framework, the existing manual procedures were analyzed, their automatability assessed, and redesigned into automated to-be processes evaluated through accuracy and time-efficiency metrics. Automatability was examined using value-complexity analysis and color-coded matrices, confirming that these tasks met the criteria for RPA integration. Results showed that the automated procedures achieved 100% accuracy in both bibliographic processing and circulation- related outputs. Time efficiency also improved significantly, with processing durations reduced by 5.11 seconds in INFOLIB and 50.66 seconds in KOHA compared to manual execution. These findings demonstrate that RPA effectively reduces staff workload, minimizes human error, and enhances operational stability in academic library environments. The study concludes that automation through PAD can serve as a practical model for modernizing library workflows and supporting digital transformation. Future research may explore automating additional library operations, improving evaluation metrics, and conducting broader testing to strengthen applicability.
